Grants are awarded to capital projects that help people live more independently.
The organization is particularly interested in projects focusing on training, employment, and supported housing.
The organization is especially interested in projects that help young people transition from children's services to adult services.
The organization is keen to hear from organizations that may struggle to raise funds from the public due to the nature of their work.
Applicant organizations must be registered charities or local authorities.
If applicable, applicant organizations must have at least a 'Good' rating from a regulator such as CQC or Ofsted.
Projects must be for a new building, refurbishment work, or equipment.
Projects must include capital costs of at least £50,000.
Projects must have a shortfall in capital funding of at least £25,000.
Projects must address at least one of the following aims: increased access to services, improved quality and range of services, or improved future sustainability of the organization.
The application process is a two-stage process.
Stage 1 applications are submitted via an online application system.
Stage 1 applications require a brief description of the project, total cost, current funding shortfall, and proposed timetable.
Stage 1 applications require confirmation of support from the Chief Executive or equivalent.
Stage 1 applications require audited accounts for the past two years.
Stage 2 applications are by invitation only.
Stage 2 applications are submitted via an online application system.
Unless otherwise agreed, at least 25% of the capital costs must be raised before submitting a Stage 2 application, unless the project cost is under £80,000.
Any necessary planning permission should be in place for Stage 2 applications.
Expert reviewers read Stage 2 applications.
Expert panels consider applications and make recommendations to trustees.
Organizations that have previously been awarded a grant must wait five years before submitting another application for a different project.
Universities and large charities with more than one site may reapply more frequently and should contact the organization before applying.
Organizations turned down at Stage 1 can submit a new application for a different project at any time.
Organizations turned down at Stage 2 must wait at least one year before submitting a new application for a different project.
The same project is not normally considered twice.

Round 1 Stage 1 applications open on November 20th and close on January 5th.
Round 1 Stage 2 applications close on March 1st.
Round 1 funding decisions are made in June.
Round 2 Stage 1 applications open on May 14th and close on July 1st.
Round 2 Stage 2 applications close on September 1st.
Round 2 funding decisions are made in December.
If a deadline falls on a weekend, applications received by 9 am on the following Monday are accepted.
Grants are not made retrospectively; projects must be ongoing at the time of a funding decision.
An invitation to Stage 2 remains open for three funding rounds unless otherwise agreed.
The applicant and project location must be in the UK.
The minimum grant amount is £25,000.
The usual grant range is £40,000 – £75,000.
Match funding may be required if the project cost is between £50,000 to £80,000.
Projects costing above £80,000 require at least 25% match funding when submitting a Stage 2 application.
Funding decisions are made in June and December annually.
Projects must not be completed before a funding decision is made.
The Wolfson funding programme is for Health & Disability.
